raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

The P2P offload client identified a load by `kv_request_id` and `round_seq`. After abort-ack timeout, idle request state was deleted, so a later request that reused the same id started again at round 0. A delayed `AbortAck` or `TransferDone` for the old generation then completed the new load.

This change allocates `round_seq` from one session-wide counter. Rounds are never reused for the session's life, so a retired round cannot match a later load — for any id, not just pruned-and-reused ones — in O(1) memory.

## Changes
- `session/client.py`: `_alloc_round()` seeds each new request and advances after each fetch; drop the per-id `_next_round` map.
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py`: late abort-ack and transfer-done after id reuse must not complete the new load; the new round's own transfer-done still succeeds; 1000 completed unique ids leave no per-id round state, and reusing the first id still rejects the retired round.

## Codepath coverage
- `collect_results` abort-ack timeout → `_on_load_terminal` → `_maybe_prune` → reuse → `on_abort_ack`: ignored.
- Same prune → reuse → `on_transfer_done` (old round): ignored.
- Same prune → reuse → `on_transfer_done` (new round): completes the new job.
- `on_abort_ack` / successful `on_transfer_done` prune of a first-generation id: still drops `_requests`; first-generation completions unchanged.
- Successful `TransferDone` of 1000 unique ids: `_requests` empty, no per-id round map.
- HTTP/gRPC inference that uses `OffloadingConnector` P2P all dispatch through `ClientRole` `on_abort_ack` / `on_transfer_done`.

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open and merged PRs for `kv_request_id`, `_maybe_prune`, `round_seq`, P2P abort-ack, and `ClientRole`.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53453 tombs reaped **producer** stores so a late **FetchMsg** fails in one RTT; it does not retain client `round_seq` after abort-ack prune.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49877 (merged) introduced per-round client loads; it still prunes idle state and restarts at 0.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55182 validates role sub-dict types; different control.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51504 bounds P2P ZMQ sessions; different control.

## Tests
- `test_late_abort_ack_after_id_reuse_does_not_complete_new_load`
- `test_late_transfer_done_after_id_reuse_does_not_complete_new_load`
- `test_session_round_allocator_is_o1_and_never_reuses_rounds`

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py -q --noconftest
```

104 passed.

nodes.body:
This change breaks PD after the first request on a session.

_alloc_round() takes rounds from one counter shared by the whole session. So every kv_request_id after the first gets round 2, 4, and so on. The PD server side still only uses round 0: submit_store → add_stored_blocks doesn't pass a round, so the stored blocks always land in outbound[0].

For a second PD request on the same session, the decoder sends FetchMsg(round_seq=2) and its request lands in outbound[2]. The prefiller's blocks are in outbound[0], so the two never match and no TransferDone is sent. The load waits out the 30s timeout and fails. The new tests only cover the lookup path, where the round comes from LookupMsg, so they don't catch this.

Suggested fix: keep rounds per kv_request_id and don't reset them on prune, or keep PD clients (ones that never probed) on round 0. Please also add a test that runs two or more PD requests on one session.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @jperezdealgaba.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

2 blocking comments:
1. _next_round grows without bound for the process lifetime
2. The else 1 fallback retains entries that protect nothing

Suggested fix for both: session-global monotonic round allocator

Allocate round_seq from one session-wide counter instead of per-id. Rounds are then never reused for the session's life, so a retired round can never match a live load — for every id, not just pruned-and-reused ones — in O(1) memory, with no map, TTL, or debug counter:

def _alloc_round(self) -> int:
    round_seq = self._round_alloc
    self._round_alloc += 1
    return round_seq

_get_or_create_request seeds round_seq=self._alloc_round(); request_blocks does st.round_seq = self._alloc_round() instead of += 1. 12 insertions, 2 deletions.

_next_round grows without bound for the process lifetime.
close() is the only thing that clears it, and sessions are only dropped when the peer connection dies (manager.py:681) — in a healthy deployment, the lifetime of the process. At ~110 bytes/entry (38-char id + dict slot), per peer session: ~0.95 GB/day at 100 req/s, ~9.5 GB/day at 1000 req/s.

The else 1 fallback retains entries that protect nothing
st.round_seq == 0 means no fetch was ever issued for this id — round_seq only advances in request_blocks — so no TransferDone/AbortAck for round 0 can exist. Verified: a pure-lookup request that missed and never fetched still leaves _next_round={'req-miss': 1}. In symmetric-P2P mode the map therefore grows one entry per request regardless of hit or miss, not "one int per unique completed id" as the PR body states. Gating on st.round_seq > 0 removes that class at no cost to the fix.

issue_comments.body:
This change breaks PD after the first request on a session.

_alloc_round() takes rounds from one counter shared by the whole session. So every kv_request_id after the first gets round 2, 4, and so on. The PD server side still only uses round 0: submit_store → add_stored_blocks doesn't pass a round, so the stored blocks always land in outbound[0].

For a second PD request on the same session, the decoder sends FetchMsg(round_seq=2) and its request lands in outbound[2]. The prefiller's blocks are in outbound[0], so the two never match and no TransferDone is sent. The load waits out the 30s timeout and fails. The new tests only cover the lookup path, where the round comes from LookupMsg, so they don't catch this.

Suggested fix: keep rounds per kv_request_id and don't reset them on prune, or keep PD clients (ones that never probed) on round 0. Please also add a test that runs two or more PD requests on one session.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

2 blocking comments:
1. _next_round grows without bound for the process lifetime
2. The else 1 fallback retains entries that protect nothing

Suggested fix for both: session-global monotonic round allocator

Allocate round_seq from one session-wide counter instead of per-id. Rounds are then never reused for the session's life, so a retired round can never match a live load — for every id, not just pruned-and-reused ones — in O(1) memory, with no map, TTL, or debug counter:

def _alloc_round(self) -> int:
    round_seq = self._round_alloc
    self._round_alloc += 1
    return round_seq

_get_or_create_request seeds round_seq=self._alloc_round(); request_blocks does st.round_seq = self._alloc_round() instead of += 1. 12 insertions, 2 deletions.
